title: unity_catalog: the vended endpoint_url is ignored
description: For each table it reads, the `unity_catalog` extension asks the catalog for temporary credentials and creates an internal S3 secret with them (`__internal_uc_<table id>`, scoped to the table's location). It does not take the `endpoint_url` the catalog vends with them (an S3-compatible store such as MinIO), so the reads go to AWS and fail with `InvalidAccessKeyId`.
Workaround: DuckDB's global S3 settings, which the internal secret falls back to: `SET s3_endpoint='host:port'`, `SET s3_url_style='path'`, `SET s3_use_ssl=false` for plain HTTP, `SET s3_region=...`.

provenance.checked_by: homelab catalog session (AlexanderNenninger/homelab#9): DuckDB 2.0.0 in Python, extensions unity_catalog cc59382f52, delta 9dcfb65b99, httpfs 77392a7207, against Unity Catalog OSS 0.7.0 with unitycatalog/unitycatalog#1959 on MinIO

evidence.sql: ATTACH 'homelab' AS lake (TYPE unity_catalog); SELECT count(*) FROM lake.ci.job_commits
evidence.observed: HTTP 403 listing 's3://metrics/ci/job_commits/_delta_log/': InvalidAccessKeyId: The AWS Access Key Id you provided does not exist in our records (an AWS response; the catalog vended MinIO keys with endpoint_url http://minio:9000)

evidence.sql: SELECT name, type, scope FROM duckdb_secrets()
SET s3_endpoint='minio:9000'; SET s3_url_style='path'; SET s3_use_ssl=false; SET s3_region='us-east-1'; then the same SELECT
evidence.observed: the reads reach MinIO (and stop at duckdb-IO3)
